newsitem.title: HONG KONG: MGM to beam its old movies to Asian cable viewers.
newsitem.headline: MGM to beam its old movies to Asian cable viewers.

text.p: Hollywood's MGM film studio on Wednesday launched a satellite channel that beams sanitised versions of well-worn MGM movies such as "The Great Escape", "West Side Story" and "Rocky" into Asian homes.
"A repeat is only a repeat if you have seen it before," Gary Marenzi, president of MGM/UA Telecommunications Group said at a cable and satellite conference in Hong Kong.
The Hollywood film studio began broadcasting the 24-hour channel, called MGM Gold, via a Malaysian MEASAT satellite on November 1.

The channel was formally launched on Wednesday with the announcement that distribution agreements had been reached in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore and Indonesia. It is not on offer anywhere else in the world.

MGM is banking that many of its films have not yet been seen in the region. It also hopes its movies, which will be censored to conform with cultural sensitivities in the region, will appeal to Asian families.
MGM Gold is the latest Western channel to launch in Asia relying on advertising and subscription revenue to make money.
Initially, revenues will come mainly from cable subscribers, but eventually the channel hopes to interrupt programming with advertising to increase revenue.
The channel will be available via cable-TV providers and will likely compete in some markets with Home Box Office, or HBO, an American cable movie channel featuring some of the latest movies.
But officials representing the new channel say the Hollywood cachet associated with the MGM name should help it win viewers.
"It's (HBO) a nice brand but it doesn't have that same connection to Hollywood that we have," said Bill Lee, senior vice president of MGM/UA.
The channel will also show more recent MGM movies such as "Get Shorty".

MGM Gold's films will comply with some of Asia's toughest censorship standards. They have to be approved by Malaysia's strict government censors before being uplinked to the satellite for Asian distribution, channel officials said.
"There will be things we have to bleep out of certain films," Marenzi told reporters later at a news conference.
Films will be in English and carry Chinese, Indonesian and Thai subtitles, where appropriate.
The encrypted channel, which viewers can only receive with a decoder box, aims to launch in India next year.
The film studio has a library of 1,600 movies to draw on.
"Most of them are colour and most of them appeal to families," Marenzi said.
The channel is a 50-50 joint venture between MGM and the international arm of programmer Encore Media Corp.
Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc is jointly owned by American investor Kirk Kerkorian's company Tracinda Corp and Australian media concern Seven Network Ltd.
Encore International is jointly owned by Tele-Communications Inc and private interests.
